description: Sporting rules per season that change race strategy (H1, D-053). source_type historical_verified: each rule is from the sources below. 2000-2009 (refuelling era) is added in H1b.

rule_sources.points: 25-18-15-12-10-8-6-4-2-1 since 2010 (FIA sporting regulations; Motorsport Week on the 2025 return to the 2010-2018 structure)
rule_sources.fastest_lap_point: 2019-2024, only if the driver finishes in the top 10; scrapped for 2025 by the WMSC in October 2024 (formula1.com/en/latest/article/fastest-lap-point-to-be-scrapped-in-2025-after-latest-fia-world-motor-sport.4pUjDzWnGRN7KVWENLc1BY)
rule_sources.double_points_final_round: 2014 Abu Dhabi GP only (2014 FIA sporting regulations)
rule_sources.shortened_race_points: half points below 75 % distance until 2021; sliding scale from 2022 after the 2021 Belgian GP (motorsportmagazine.com/articles/single-seaters/f1/f1-reveals-new-short-race-points-system-to-avoid-spa-repeat)
rule_sources.min_distinct_dry_compounds: two dry compounds must be used unless a wet tyre is used, since 2007 (FIA sporting regulations)
rule_sources.top10_start_tyres: 2010-2013 Q3 tyres, 2014-2021 Q2 tyres, free from 2022 (auto123.com/en/news/f1-top-ten-must-use-qualifying-tyres-in-2010/6429; racefans.net/2022/02/18/f1s-q3-tyre-rule-which-drivers-claimed-helped-top-teams-is-dropped-for-2022)
rule_sources.tyre_supplier: Bridgestone until 2010, Pirelli from 2011 (the-race.com, Bridgestone F1 history)
rule_sources.vsc: approved for 2015 after tests at the final 2014 events; first used at the 2015 Monaco GP (fia.com/news/world-motor-sport-council-2014-doha)
